raw:
I picked the experiments as matched pairs. Each pair applies the same edit to two parents that differ mainly in the conditioning edge, so any difference in effect isolates an interaction. The pairs probe these conditions:

- **Reachability:**
  - Edits on edge 5 are tested with node 2 live vs. dead (edges 1 and 2 none vs. not).
  - Edits on edges 2 and 4 are tested with edge 0 none vs. not.
  - Edits on edges 1 and 2 are tested with edge 5 none vs. not.
- **Residual dependence:** edits are tested with edge 3 as skip_connect vs. none. Conv upgrades, pools, pruning and skip additions may matter more when no residual exists.
- **What the edit replaces (k = j):**
  - an op replacing none vs. pool vs. skip vs. conv;
  - skip on edge 3 replacing none vs. conv3x3.
- **Parent quality:** the same edit is applied to strong (all-conv3x3) parents vs. weak (all-pool, all-skip, all-conv1x1) parents.
- **Path redundancy:** pruning (→ none) is tested with alternative paths present vs. absent.
